papers.title: An exact algorithm with a new upper bound and reductions for maximum edge weighted clique in massive sparse graphs
papers.abstract: The Maximum Edge Weighted Clique (MEWC) problem is a classic NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem with applications in network analysis, bioinformatics, and social network mining. This paper presents a novel exact algorithm that incorporates a new upper bound and reduction rules specifically designed for massive sparse graphs. The proposed algorithm leverages a divide-and-conquer strategy combined with branch-and-bound techniques that utilize the new upper bound to prune unpromising search subspaces effectively. Extensive computational experiments on large-scale real-world sparse graphs demonstrate that the algorithm significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, solving instances with up to millions of vertices that were previously intractable.
